extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political theory, comparative politics, and history
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing the distinct social, geographic, legal, institutional, moral, and religious causes the author identifies as contributing to the maintenance (or endangerment) of a democratic republic, with emphasis on the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger from the size and nature of cities
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of certain American cities, and especially the nature of their population, is a real danger which threatens the future security of the democratic republics of the New World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cities act as large assemblies where inhabitants can concert together and awaken mutual excitement, prompting sudden and passionate resolutions; the populace exercises prodigious influence upon magistrates and frequently executes its own wishes without their intervention. The preponderance of capital cities is a serious blow upon the representative system and exposes modern republics to defects like those of ancient republics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of an armed force under majority control
rubrics_metrics.description: The government must succeed in creating an armed force which, while it remains under the control of the majority of the nation, will be independent of the town population and able to repress its excesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An armed force controlled by the majority (not the towns) is presented as a mitigating instrument against urban populace excesses; without such a force, the influence of cities could imperil the republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of settlements and equality of conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of the American settlements may be looked upon as the first and most efficacious cause to which the present prosperity of the United States may be attributed: their forefathers imported that equality of conditions into the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early settlers bequeathed customs, manners, and opinions that contribute most to the success of a republican form of government; the author even personifies the destiny of America in the first Puritan settler.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territory and natural resources enabling equality and freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: God himself gave [Americans] the means of remaining equal and free by placing them upon a boundless continent that is open to their exertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical causes independent of laws (fertile soil, inexhaustible resources, never-failing rivers) promote general prosperity and are especially favorable to the stability of a democratic constitution because abundance reduces pressures that produce unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unoccupied land and absence of populous hostile nations
rubrics_metrics.description: North America was, properly speaking, an empty continent awaiting its inhabitants rather than a land occupied by well-established peoples who had to be subjugated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because settlers did not need to extirpate or subdue a large existing population, colonization could proceed without the destructive conflicts that accompanied many other state-foundings; this peaceful settlement favored prosperity and republican institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous emigration and westward expansion preventing overpopulation and property parcelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous removal of the human race toward the West causes populations of older states to increase slowly and prevents the parcelling out of estates; emigration supplies land and opportunity and keeps estates from being subdivided to excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European and American emigrants alike move Westward; this double emigration ensures land is available, enabling younger sons and laborers to find fortunes and preventing the social ills that arise when parcels become too small to support families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws favorable to division of property tempered by circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws of the United States are extremely favorable to the division of property; but a cause more powerful than the laws prevents property from being divided to excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although statutory changes (abolition of primogeniture) facilitate division, social and geographic circumstances (availability of land, emigration) lead in practice to re-establishing de facto primogeniture (eldest son takes land) without legal coercion, avoiding the dangers of excessive fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restless pursuit of prosperity and emigration as stabilizing passions
rubrics_metrics.description: A restless disposition, an unbounded desire of riches, and an excessive love of independence — though often seen as vices in Europe — are elements which ensure a long and peaceful duration to the republics of America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These passions disperse the population across the continent, prevent overconcentration, and turn what might be social vices into forces that support republican stability by providing outlets (land, commerce) for ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial habits shaping political character
rubrics_metrics.description: The passions which agitate the Americans most deeply are their commercial passions; they introduce business habits into political life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Americans value order, regular conduct, good sense that amasses fortunes, practice over theory, and positive calculations rather than grand generalities; these commercial traits foster political stability and a preference for practical governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of prosperity on opinions and political conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosperity acts upon conduct and opinion; men who become rich change their views with their fortune, and happy circumstances furnish decisive arguments that previously were lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author observes that prosperity causes individuals (including former radicals) to embrace order, obedience to laws, and support for institutions that protect property and peace; prosperity thus shapes civic attitudes favorable to republican maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal constitution combining empire power with small-state security
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal form of government enables the Union to combine the power of a great empire with the security of a small state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federalism is identified as one of the three principal circumstances that most powerfully contribute to maintaining the democratic republic in the United States by balancing centralized strength and local security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal institutions limiting despotism of the majority
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal institutions limit the despotism of the majority and, at the same time, impart a taste for freedom and a knowledge of the art of being free to the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local self-government inculcates habits and skills of freedom and civic participation, acting as a check on majority tyranny while educating citizens in democratic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution of the judicial power as a check on democratic excesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The constitution of the judicial power serves to repress the excesses of democracy and to check and direct the impulses of the majority without stopping its activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts function as institutional moderators that restrain majority excesses through legal adjudication, thereby preserving rule of law while allowing democratic action to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners (mores) as a sustaining cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners — understood as the whole moral and intellectual condition of a people, including notions, opinions, and ideas — are one of the general causes to which the maintenance of a democratic republic in the United States is attributable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author intends to point out features of American manners that are favorable to political institutions: habits, common opinions, and the mental character of the populace contribute deeply to institutional stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion considered as a political institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Every religion is connected with a political opinion by affinity; in North America many inhabitants professed a democratic and republican Christianity which powerfully contributed to the establishment of a democracy and a republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious beliefs and structures influence temporal institutions; in the U.S., religious sects generally harmonize with laws and support civic order, thereby reinforcing democratic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catholicism's unexpected affinity with equality of conditions in America
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrary to common belief, Catholicism in the United States tends to be one of the religions most favorable to the equality of conditions: within the Church the lay faithful are equal beneath a priesthood separated from civil power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the priesthood is separated from government in the U.S., Catholics — often poor and a political minority — naturally favor institutions open to all citizens; doctrinal uniformity and clerical separation reduce aristocratic tendencies and incline Catholics toward democratic and republican principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical and religious reinforcement of civic solidarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clergy of different sects generally hold opinions consonant to the laws; religious discourse often appeals to national liberty and supports civic causes (example: priests addressing public meetings to aid foreign liberty movements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious leaders, by aligning spiritual and civic rhetoric, help create a unified current of public opinion that bolsters the laws and the democratic order rather than undermining them.
